08.59c87dbdb0:
<n>83:2</n> Quam dilécta tabernácula tua, Dómine virtútum: * concupíscit, et déficit ánima mea in átria Dómini.
<n>83:3</n> Cor meum, et caro mea * exsultavérunt in Deum vivum.
<n>83:4</n> Étenim passer invénit sibi domum: * et turtur nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos.
<n>83:4</n> Altária tua, Dómine virtútum: * Rex meus, et Deus meus.
<n>83:5</n> Beáti, qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine: * in sǽcula sæculórum laudábunt te.
<n>83:6</n> Beátus vir, cujus est auxílium abs te: * ascensiónes in corde suo dispósuit, in valle lacrimárum in loco, quem pósuit.
<n>83:8</n> Étenim benedictiónem dabit legislátor, ibunt de virtúte in virtútem: * vidébitur Deus deórum in Sion.
<n>83:9</n> Dómine, Deus virtútum, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe, Deus Jacob.
<n>83:10</n> Protéctor noster, áspice, Deus: * et réspice in fáciem Christi tui:
<n>83:11</n> Quia mélior est dies una in átriis tuis, * super míllia.
<n>83:11</n> Elégi abjéctus esse in domo Dei mei: * magis quam habitáre in tabernáculis peccatórum.
<n>83:12</n> Quia misericórdiam, et veritátem díligit Deus: * grátiam et glóriam dabit Dóminus.
<n>83:13</n> Non privábit bonis eos, qui ámbulant in innocéntia: * Dómine virtútum, beátus homo, qui sperat in te.
08.63d9e1065a:
<n>83:2</n> How lovely are thy tabernacles, O Lord of hosts! * my soul longeth and fainteth for the courts of the Lord.
<n>83:3</n> My heart and my flesh * have rejoiced in the living God.
<n>83:4</n> For the sparrow hath found herself a house, * and the turtledove a nest for herself where she may lay her young ones:
<n>83:4</n> Thy altars, O Lord of hosts, * my king and my God.
<n>83:5</n> Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: * they shall praise thee for ever and ever.
<n>83:6</n> Blessed is the man whose help is from thee: * in his heart he hath disposed to ascend by steps, in the vale of tears, in the place which he hath set.
<n>83:8</n> For the lawgiver shall give a blessing, they shall go from virtue to virtue: * the God of gods shall be seen in Sion.
<n>83:9</n> O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer: * give ear, O God of Jacob.
<n>83:10</n> Behold, O God our protector: * and look on the face of thy Christ.
<n>83:11</n> For better is one day in thy courts * above thousands.
<n>83:11</n> I have chosen to be an abject in the house of my God, * rather than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners.
<n>83:12</n> For God loveth mercy and truth: * the Lord will give grace and glory.
<n>83:13</n> He will not deprive of good things them that walk in innocence: * O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that trusteth in thee.
08.b2113150f7:
<n>89:1</n> Dómine, refúgium factus es nobis: * a generatióne in generatiónem.
<n>89:2</n> Priúsquam montes fíerent, aut formarétur terra et orbis: * a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum tu es, Deus.
<n>89:3</n> Ne avértas hóminem in humilitátem: * et dixísti: Convertímini, fílii hóminum.
<n>89:4</n> Quóniam mille anni ante óculos tuos, * tamquam dies hestérna, quæ prætériit,
<n>89:5</n> Et custódia in nocte, * quæ pro níhilo habéntur, eórum anni erunt.
<n>89:6</n> Mane sicut herba tránseat, mane flóreat, et tránseat: * véspere décidat, indúret et aréscat.
<n>89:7</n> Quia defécimus in ira tua, * et in furóre tuo turbáti sumus.
<n>89:8</n> Posuísti iniquitátes nostras in conspéctu tuo: * sǽculum nostrum in illuminatióne vultus tui.
<n>89:9</n> Quóniam omnes dies nostri defecérunt: * et in ira tua defécimus.
<n>89:9</n> Anni nostri sicut aránea meditabúntur: * dies annórum nostrórum in ipsis, septuagínta anni.
<n>89:10</n> Si autem in potentátibus, octogínta anni: * et ámplius eórum, labor et dolor.
<n>89:10</n> Quóniam supervénit mansuetúdo: * et corripiémur.
<n>89:11</n> Quis novit potestátem iræ tuæ: * et præ timóre tuo iram tuam dinumeráre?
<n>89:12</n> Déxteram tuam sic notam fac: * et erudítos corde in sapiéntia.
<n>89:13</n> Convértere, Dómine, úsquequo? * et deprecábilis esto super servos tuos.
<n>89:14</n> Repléti sumus mane misericórdia tua: * et exsultávimus, et delectáti sumus ómnibus diébus nostris.
<n>89:15</n> Lætáti sumus pro diébus, quibus nos humiliásti: * annis, quibus vídimus mala.
<n>89:16</n> Réspice in servos tuos, et in ópera tua: * et dírige fílios eórum.
<n>89:17</n> Et sit splendor Dómini, Dei nostri, super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos: * et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.
08.be8b1f0b84:
<n>89:1</n> Lord, thou hast been our refuge * from generation to generation.
<n>89:2</n> Before the mountains were made, or the earth and the world was formed; * from eternity and to eternity thou art God.
<n>89:3</n> Turn not man away to be brought low: * and thou hast said: Be converted, O ye sons of men.
<n>89:4</n> For a thousand years in thy sight * are as yesterday, which is past.
<n>89:5</n> And as a watch in the night, * things that are counted nothing, shall their years be.
<n>89:6</n> In the morning man shall grow up like grass; in the morning he shall flourish and pass away: * in the evening he shall fall, grow dry, and wither.
<n>89:7</n> For in thy wrath we have fainted away: * and are troubled in thy indignation.
<n>89:8</n> Thou hast set our iniquities before thy eyes: * our life in the light of thy countenance.
<n>89:9</n> For all our days are spent; * and in thy wrath we have fainted away.
<n>89:9</n> Our years shall be considered as a spider: * the days of our years in them are threescore and ten years.
<n>89:10</n> But if in the strong they be fourscore years: * and what is more of them is labour and sorrow.
<n>89:10</n> For mildness is come upon us: * and we shall be corrected.
<n>89:11</n> Who knoweth the power of thy anger, * and for thy fear can number thy wrath?
<n>89:12</n> So make thy right hand known: * and men learned in heart, in wisdom.
<n>89:13</n> Return, O Lord, how long? * and be entreated in favour of thy servants.
<n>89:14</n> We are filled in the morning with thy mercy: * and we have rejoiced, and are delighted all our days.
<n>89:15</n> We have rejoiced for the days in which thou hast humbled us: * for the years in which we have seen evils.
<n>89:16</n> Look upon thy servants and upon their works: * and direct their children.
<n>89:17</n> And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us: and direct thou the works of our hands over us; * yea, the work of our hands do thou direct.
08.241ec428b0:
<n>80:2</n> Exsultáte Deo, adjutóri nostro: * jubiláte Deo Jacob.
<n>80:3</n> Súmite psalmum, et date týmpanum: * psaltérium jucúndum cum cíthara.
<n>80:4</n> Buccináte in Neoménia tuba, * in insígni die solemnitátis vestræ.
<n>80:5</n> Quia præcéptum in Israël est: * et judícium Deo Jacob.
<n>80:6</n> Testimónium in Joseph pósuit illud, cum exíret de terra Ægýpti: * linguam, quam non nóverat, audívit.
<n>80:7</n> Divértit ab onéribus dorsum ejus: * manus ejus in cóphino serviérunt.
<n>80:8</n> In tribulatióne invocásti me, et liberávi te: * exaudívi te in abscóndito tempestátis: probávi te apud aquam contradictiónis.
<n>80:9</n> Audi, pópulus meus, et contestábor te: * Israël, si audíeris me, non erit in te deus recens, neque adorábis deum aliénum.
<n>80:11</n> Ego enim sum Dóminus Deus tuus, qui edúxi te de terra Ægýpti: * diláta os tuum, et implébo illud.
<n>80:12</n> Et non audívit pópulus meus vocem meam: * et Israël non inténdit mihi.
<n>80:13</n> Et dimísi eos secúndum desidéria cordis eórum: * ibunt in adinventiónibus suis.
<n>80:14</n> Si pópulus meus audísset me: * Israël si in viis meis ambulásset:
<n>80:15</n> Pro níhilo fórsitan inimícos eórum humiliássem: * et super tribulántes eos misíssem manum meam.
<n>80:16</n> Inimíci Dómini mentíti sunt ei: * et erit tempus eórum in sǽcula.
<n>80:17</n> Et cibávit eos ex ádipe fruménti: * et de petra, melle saturávit eos.
08.011c8db51d:
<n>80:2</n> Rejoice to God, our helper: * sing aloud to the God of Jacob.
<n>80:3</n> Take a psalm, and bring hither the timbrel: * the pleasant psaltery with the harp.
<n>80:4</n> Blow up the trumpet on the new moon, * on the noted day of your solemnity.
<n>80:5</n> For it is a commandment in Israel, * and a judgment to the God of Jacob.
<n>80:6</n> He ordained it for a testimony in Joseph, when he came out of the land of Egypt: * he heard a tongue which he knew not.
<n>80:7</n> He removed his back from the burdens: * his hands had served in baskets.
<n>80:8</n> Thou calledst upon me in affliction, and I delivered thee: * I heard thee in the secret place of tempest: I proved thee at the waters of contradiction.
<n>80:9</n> Hear, O my people, and I will testify to thee: * O Israel, if thou wilt hearken to me; there shall be no new god in thee: neither shalt thou adore a strange god.
<n>80:11</n> For I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt: * open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.
<n>80:12</n> But my people heard not my voice: * and Israel hearkened not to me.
<n>80:13</n> So I let them go according to the desires of their heart: * they shall walk in their own inventions.
<n>80:14</n> If my people had heard me: * if Israel had walked in my ways:
<n>80:15</n> I should soon have humbled their enemies, * and laid my hand on them that troubled them.
<n>80:16</n> The enemies of the Lord have lied to him: * and their time shall be for ever.
<n>80:17</n> And he fed them with the fat of wheat, * and filled them with honey out of the rock.
08.62df94e230:
<n>82:2</n> Deus, quis símilis erit tibi? * Ne táceas, neque compescáris, Deus.
<n>82:3</n> Quóniam ecce inimíci tui sonuérunt: * et qui odérunt te extulérunt caput.
<n>82:4</n> Super pópulum tuum malignavérunt consílium: * et cogitavérunt advérsus sanctos tuos.
<n>82:5</n> Dixérunt: Veníte, et disperdámus eos de gente: * et non memorétur nomen Israël ultra.
<n>82:6</n> Quóniam cogitavérunt unanímiter: * simul advérsum te testaméntum disposuérunt, tabernácula Idumæórum et Ismahelítæ:
<n>82:8</n> Moab, et Agaréni, Gebal, et Ammon, et Ámalec: * alienígenæ cum habitántibus Tyrum.
<n>82:9</n> Étenim Assur venit cum illis: * facti sunt in adjutórium fíliis Lot.
<n>82:10</n> Fac illis sicut Mádian, et Sísaræ: * sicut Jabin in torrénte Cisson.
<n>82:11</n> Disperiérunt in Endor: * facti sunt ut stercus terræ.
<n>82:12</n> Pone príncipes eórum sicut Oreb, et Zeb, * et Zébee, et Sálmana:
<n>82:13</n> Omnes príncipes eórum: * qui dixérunt: Hereditáte possideámus Sanctuárium Dei.
<n>82:14</n> Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam: * et sicut stípulam ante fáciem venti.
<n>82:15</n> Sicut ignis, qui combúrit silvam: * et sicut flamma combúrens montes:
<n>82:16</n> Ita persequéris illos in tempestáte tua: * et in ira tua turbábis eos.
<n>82:17</n> Imple fácies eórum ignomínia: * et quærent nomen tuum, Dómine.
<n>82:18</n> Erubéscant, et conturbéntur in sǽculum sǽculi: * et confundántur, et péreant.
<n>82:19</n> Et cognóscant quia nomen tibi Dóminus: * tu solus Altíssimus in omni terra.
08.001e055faa:
<n>82:2</n> O God, who shall be like to thee? * Hold not thy peace, neither be thou still, O God.
<n>82:3</n> For lo, thy enemies have made a noise: * and they that hate thee have lifted up the head.
<n>82:4</n> They have taken a malicious counsel against thy people, * and have consulted against thy saints.
<n>82:5</n> They have said: Come and let us destroy them, * so that they be not a nation: and let the name of Israel be remembered no more.
<n>82:6</n> For they have contrived with one consent: * they have made a covenant together against thee; the tabernacles of the Edomites, and the Ismahelites:
<n>82:8</n> Moab, and the Agarens, Gebal, and Ammon and Amalec: * the Philistines, with the inhabitants of Tyre.
<n>82:9</n> Yea, and the Assyrian also is joined with them: * they are come to the aid of the sons of Lot.
<n>82:10</n> Do to them as thou didst to Madian and to Sisara: * as to Jabin at the brook of Cisson.
<n>82:11</n> Who perished at Endor: * and became as dung for the earth.
<n>82:12</n> Make their princes like Oreb, and Zeb, * and Zebee, and Salmana.
<n>82:13</n> All their princes, * who have said: Let us possess the sanctuary of God for an inheritance.
<n>82:14</n> O my God, make them like a wheel; * and as stubble before the wind.
<n>82:15</n> As fire which burneth the wood: * and as a flame burning mountains:
<n>82:16</n> So shalt thou pursue them with thy tempest: * and shalt trouble them in thy wrath.
<n>82:17</n> Fill their faces with shame; * and they shall seek thy name, O Lord.
<n>82:18</n> Let them be ashamed and troubled for ever and ever: * and let them be confounded and perish.
<n>82:19</n> And let them know that the Lord is thy name: * thou alone art the most High over all the earth.
08.ba9bbd4310:
<n>84:2</n> Benedixísti, Dómine, terram tuam: * avertísti captivitátem Jacob.
<n>84:3</n> Remisísti iniquitátem plebis tuæ: * operuísti ómnia peccáta eórum.
<n>84:4</n> Mitigásti omnem iram tuam: * avertísti ab ira indignatiónis tuæ.
<n>84:5</n> Convérte nos, Deus, salutáris noster: * et avérte iram tuam a nobis.
<n>84:6</n> Numquid in ætérnum irascéris nobis? * aut exténdes iram tuam a generatióne in generatiónem?
<n>84:7</n> Deus, tu convérsus vivificábis nos: * et plebs tua lætábitur in te.
<n>84:8</n> Osténde nobis, Dómine, misericórdiam tuam: * et salutáre tuum da nobis.
<n>84:9</n> Áudiam quid loquátur in me Dóminus Deus: * quóniam loquétur pacem in plebem suam.
<n>84:9</n> Et super sanctos suos: * et in eos, qui convertúntur ad cor.
<n>84:10</n> Verúmtamen prope timéntes eum salutáre ipsíus: * ut inhábitet glória in terra nostra.
<n>84:11</n> Misericórdia, et véritas obviavérunt sibi: * justítia, et pax osculátæ sunt.
<n>84:12</n> Véritas de terra orta est: * et justítia de cælo prospéxit.
<n>84:13</n> Étenim Dóminus dabit benignitátem: * et terra nostra dabit fructum suum.
<n>84:14</n> Justítia ante eum ambulábit: * et ponet in via gressus suos.
08.1a38459cbe:
<n>84:2</n> Lord, thou hast blessed thy land: * thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob.
<n>84:3</n> Thou hast forgiven the iniquity of thy people: * thou hast covered all their sins.
<n>84:4</n> Thou hast mitigated all thy anger: * thou hast turned away from the wrath of thy indignation.
<n>84:5</n> Convert us, O God our saviour: * and turn off thy anger from us.
<n>84:6</n> Wilt thou be angry with us for ever: * or wilt thou extend thy wrath from generation to generation?
<n>84:7</n> Thou wilt turn, O God, and bring us to life: * and thy people shall rejoice in thee.
<n>84:8</n> Shew us, O Lord, thy mercy; * and grant us thy salvation.
<n>84:9</n> I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me: * for he will speak peace.
<n>84:9</n> And unto his saints: * and unto them that are converted to the heart.
<n>84:10</n> Surely his salvation is near to them that fear him: * that glory may dwell in our land.
<n>84:11</n> Mercy and truth have met each other: * justice and peace have kissed.
<n>84:12</n> Truth is sprung out of the earth: * and justice hath looked down from heaven.
<n>84:13</n> For the Lord will give goodness: * and our earth shall yield her fruit.
<n>84:14</n> Justice shall walk before him: * and shall set his steps in the way.
08.d1fd62ee46:
<n>81:1</n> Deus stetit in synagóga deórum: * in médio autem deos dijúdicat.
<n>81:2</n> Úsquequo judicátis iniquitátem: * et fácies peccatórum súmitis?
<n>81:3</n> Judicáte egéno, et pupíllo: * húmilem, et páuperem justificáte.
<n>81:4</n> Erípite páuperem: * et egénum de manu peccatóris liberáte.
<n>81:5</n> Nesciérunt, neque intellexérunt, in ténebris ámbulant: * movebúntur ómnia fundaménta terræ.
<n>81:6</n> Ego dixi: Dii estis, * et fílii Excélsi omnes.
<n>81:7</n> Vos autem sicut hómines moriémini: * et sicut unus de princípibus cadétis.
<n>81:8</n> Surge, Deus, júdica terram: * quóniam tu hereditábis in ómnibus géntibus.
08.259982ab63:
<n>81:1</n> God hath stood in the congregation of gods: * and being in the midst of them he judgeth gods.
<n>81:2</n> How long will you judge unjustly: * and accept the persons of the wicked?
<n>81:3</n> Judge for the needy and fatherless: * do justice to the humble and the poor.
<n>81:4</n> Rescue the poor; * and deliver the needy out of the hand of the sinner.
<n>81:5</n> They have not known nor understood: they walk on in darkness: * all the foundations of the earth shall be moved.
<n>81:6</n> I have said: You are gods * and all of you the sons of the most High.
<n>81:7</n> But you like men shall die: * and shall fall like one of the princes.
<n>81:8</n> Arise, O God, judge thou the earth: * for thou shalt inherit among all the nations.

08.a744efa12b:
<n>86:1</n> Fundaménta ejus in móntibus sanctis: * díligit Dóminus portas Sion super ómnia tabernácula Jacob.
<n>86:3</n> Gloriósa dicta sunt de te, * cívitas Dei.
<n>86:4</n> Memor ero Rahab, et Babylónis * sciéntium me.
<n>86:4</n> Ecce, alienígenæ, et Tyrus, et pópulus Æthíopum, * hi fuérunt illic.
<n>86:5</n> Numquid Sion dicet: Homo, et homo natus est in ea: * et ipse fundávit eam Altíssimus?
<n>86:6</n> Dóminus narrábit in scriptúris populórum, et príncipum: * horum, qui fuérunt in ea.
<n>86:7</n> Sicut lætántium ómnium * habitátio est in te.
08.22c0b4d70a:
<n>86:1</n> The foundations thereof are in the holy mountains: * The Lord loveth the gates of Sion above all the tabernacles of Jacob.
<n>86:3</n> Glorious things are said of thee, * O city of God.
<n>86:4</n> I will be mindful of Rahab and of Babylon * knowing me.
<n>86:4</n> Behold the foreigners, and Tyre, and the people of the Ethiopians, * these were there.
<n>86:5</n> Shall not Sion say: This man and that man is born in her? * and the Highest himself hath founded her.
<n>86:6</n> The Lord shall tell in his writings of peoples and of princes, * of them that have been in her.
<n>86:7</n> The dwelling in thee * is as it were of all rejoicing.
08.586b1fc8c2:
<n>88:2</n> Misericórdias Dómini * in ætérnum cantábo.
<n>88:2</n> In generatiónem et generatiónem * annuntiábo veritátem tuam in ore meo.
<n>88:3</n> Quóniam dixísti: In ætérnum misericórdia ædificábitur in cælis: * præparábitur véritas tua in eis.
<n>88:4</n> Dispósui testaméntum eléctis meis, jurávi David, servo meo: * Usque in ætérnum præparábo semen tuum.
<n>88:5</n> Et ædificábo in generatiónem et generatiónem * sedem tuam.
<n>88:6</n> Confitebúntur cæli mirabília tua, Dómine: * étenim veritátem tuam in ecclésia sanctórum.
<n>88:7</n> Quóniam quis in núbibus æquábitur Dómino: * símilis erit Deo in fíliis Dei?
<n>88:8</n> Deus, qui glorificátur in consílio sanctórum: * magnus et terríbilis super omnes qui in circúitu ejus sunt.
<n>88:9</n> Dómine, Deus virtútum, quis símilis tibi? * potens es, Dómine, et véritas tua in circúitu tuo.
<n>88:10</n> Tu domináris potestáti maris: * motum autem flúctuum ejus tu mítigas.
<n>88:11</n> Tu humiliásti sicut vulnerátum, supérbum: * in brácchio virtútis tuæ dispersísti inimícos tuos.
<n>88:12</n> Tui sunt cæli, et tua est terra, orbem terræ et plenitúdinem ejus tu fundásti: * aquilónem, et mare tu creásti.
<n>88:13</n> Thabor et Hermon in nómine tuo exsultábunt: * tuum brácchium cum poténtia.
<n>88:14</n> Firmétur manus tua, et exaltétur déxtera tua: * justítia et judícium præparátio sedis tuæ.
<n>88:15</n> Misericórdia et véritas præcédent fáciem tuam: * beátus pópulus, qui scit jubilatiónem.
<n>88:16</n> Dómine, in lúmine vultus tui ambulábunt, et in nómine tuo exsultábunt tota die: * et in justítia tua exaltabúntur.
<n>88:18</n> Quóniam glória virtútis eórum tu es: * et in beneplácito tuo exaltábitur cornu nostrum.
<n>88:19</n> Quia Dómini est assúmptio nostra, * et Sancti Israël, regis nostri.
08.d83a1b53e1:
<n>88:2</n> The mercies of the Lord * I will sing for ever.
<n>88:2</n> I will shew forth thy truth with my mouth * to generation and generation.
<n>88:3</n> For thou hast said: Mercy shall be built up for ever in the heavens: * thy truth shall be prepared in them.
<n>88:4</n> I have made a covenant with my elect: I have sworn to David my servant: * Thy seed will I settle for ever.
<n>88:5</n> And I will build up thy throne * unto generation and generation.
<n>88:6</n> The heavens shall confess thy wonders, O Lord: * and thy truth in the church of the saints.
<n>88:7</n> For who in the clouds can be compared to the Lord: * or who among the sons of God shall be like to God?
<n>88:8</n> God, who is glorified in the assembly of the saints: * great and terrible above all them that are about him.
<n>88:9</n> O Lord God of hosts, who is like to thee? * thou art mighty, O Lord, and thy truth is round about thee.
<n>88:10</n> Thou rulest the power of the sea: * and appeasest the motion of the waves thereof.
<n>88:11</n> Thou hast humbled the proud one, as one that is slain: * with the arm of thy strength thou hast scattered thy enemies.
<n>88:12</n> Thine are the heavens, and thine is the earth: the world and the fulness thereof thou hast founded: * the north and the sea thou hast created.
<n>88:13</n> Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name: * thy arm is with might.
<n>88:14</n> Let thy hand be strengthened, and thy right hand exalted: * justice and judgment are the preparation of thy throne.
<n>88:15</n> Mercy and truth shall go before thy face: * blessed is the people that knoweth jubilation.
<n>88:16</n> They shall walk, O Lord, in the light of thy countenance: and in thy name they shall rejoice all the day, * and in thy justice they shall be exalted.
<n>88:18</n> For thou art the glory of their strength: * and in thy good pleasure shall our horn be exalted.
<n>88:19</n> For our protection is of the Lord, * and of our king the holy one of Israel.
08.a4fe2f974e:
<n>88:20</n> Tunc locútus es in visióne sanctis tuis, et dixísti: * Pósui adjutórium in poténte: et exaltávi eléctum de plebe mea.
<n>88:21</n> Invéni David, servum meum: * óleo sancto meo unxi eum.
<n>88:22</n> Manus enim mea auxiliábitur ei: * et brácchium meum confortábit eum.
<n>88:23</n> Nihil profíciet inimícus in eo, * et fílius iniquitátis non appónet nocére ei.
<n>88:24</n> Et concídam a fácie ipsíus inimícos ejus: * et odiéntes eum in fugam convértam.
<n>88:25</n> Et véritas mea, et misericórdia mea cum ipso: * et in nómine meo exaltábitur cornu ejus.
<n>88:26</n> Et ponam in mari manum ejus: * et in flumínibus déxteram ejus.
<n>88:27</n> Ipse invocábit me: Pater meus es tu: * Deus meus, et suscéptor salútis meæ.
<n>88:28</n> Et ego primogénitum ponam illum * excélsum præ régibus terræ.
<n>88:29</n> In ætérnum servábo illi misericórdiam meam: * et testaméntum meum fidéle ipsi.
<n>88:30</n> Et ponam in sǽculum sǽculi semen ejus: * et thronum ejus sicut dies cæli.
<n>88:31</n> Si autem derelíquerint fílii ejus legem meam: * et in judíciis meis non ambuláverint:
<n>88:32</n> Si justítias meas profanáverint: * et mandáta mea non custodíerint:
<n>88:33</n> Visitábo in virga iniquitátes eórum: * et in verbéribus peccáta eórum.
<n>88:34</n> Misericórdiam autem meam non dispérgam ab eo: * neque nocébo in veritáte mea:
<n>88:35</n> Neque profanábo testaméntum meum: * et quæ procédunt de lábiis meis, non fáciam írrita.
<n>88:36</n> Semel jurávi in sancto meo: Si David méntiar: * semen ejus in ætérnum manébit.
<n>88:37</n> Et thronus ejus sicut sol in conspéctu meo, * et sicut luna perfécta in ætérnum: et testis in cælo fidélis.
08.96a6e9a006:
<n>88:20</n> Then thou spokest in a vision to thy saints, and saidst: * I have laid help upon one that is mighty, and have exalted one chosen out of my people.
<n>88:21</n> I have found David my servant: * with my holy oil I have anointed him.
<n>88:22</n> For my hand shall help him: * and my arm shall strengthen him.
<n>88:23</n> The enemy shall have no advantage over him: * nor the son of iniquity have power to hurt him.
<n>88:24</n> And I will cut down his enemies before his face; * and them that hate him I will put to flight.
<n>88:25</n> And my truth and my mercy shall be with him: * and in my name shall his horn be exalted.
<n>88:26</n> And I will set his hand in the sea; * and his right hand in the rivers.
<n>88:27</n> He shall cry out to me: Thou art my father: * my God, and the support of my salvation.
<n>88:28</n> And I will make him my firstborn, * high above the kings of the earth.
<n>88:29</n> I will keep my mercy for him for ever: * and my covenant faithful to him.
<n>88:30</n> And I will make his seed to endure for evermore: * and his throne as the days of heaven.
<n>88:31</n> And if his children forsake my law, * and walk not in my judgments:
<n>88:32</n> If they profane my justices: * and keep not my commandments:
<n>88:33</n> I will visit their iniquities with a rod: * and their sins with stripes.
<n>88:34</n> But my mercy I will not take away from him: * nor will I suffer my truth to fail.
<n>88:35</n> Neither will I profane my covenant: * and the words that proceed from my mouth I will not make void.
<n>88:36</n> Once have I sworn by my holiness: I will not lie unto David: * his seed shall endure for ever.
<n>88:37</n> And his throne as the sun before me: * and as the moon perfect for ever, and a faithful witness in heaven.
08.641fe0ad51:
<n>88:39</n> Tu vero repulísti et despexísti: * distulísti Christum tuum.
<n>88:40</n> Evertísti testaméntum servi tui: * profanásti in terra Sanctuárium ejus.
<n>88:41</n> Destruxísti omnes sepes ejus: * posuísti firmaméntum ejus formídinem.
<n>88:42</n> Diripuérunt eum omnes transeúntes viam: * factus est oppróbrium vicínis suis.
<n>88:43</n> Exaltásti déxteram depriméntium eum: * lætificásti omnes inimícos ejus.
<n>88:44</n> Avertísti adjutórium gládii ejus: * et non es auxiliátus ei in bello.
<n>88:45</n> Destruxísti eum ab emundatióne: * et sedem ejus in terram collisísti.
<n>88:46</n> Minorásti dies témporis ejus: * perfudísti eum confusióne.
<n>88:47</n> Úsquequo, Dómine, avértis in finem: * exardéscet sicut ignis ira tua?
<n>88:48</n> Memoráre quæ mea substántia: * numquid enim vane constituísti omnes fílios hóminum?
<n>88:49</n> Quis est homo, qui vivet, et non vidébit mortem: * éruet ánimam suam de manu ínferi?
<n>88:50</n> Ubi sunt misericórdiæ tuæ antíquæ, Dómine, * sicut jurásti David in veritáte tua?
<n>88:51</n> Memor esto, Dómine, oppróbrii servórum tuórum * quod contínui in sinu meo multárum géntium.
<n>88:52</n> Quod exprobravérunt inimíci tui, Dómine, * quod exprobravérunt commutatiónem Christi tui.
<n>88:53</n> Benedíctus Dóminus in ætérnum: * fiat, fiat.
08.e2ab9bb2a4:
<n>88:39</n> But thou hast rejected and despised: * thou hast been angry with thy anointed.
<n>88:40</n> Thou hast overthrown the covenant of thy servant: * thou hast profaned his sanctuary on the earth.
<n>88:41</n> Thou hast broken down all his hedges: * thou hast made his strength fear.
<n>88:42</n> All that pass by the way have robbed him: * he is become a reproach to his neighbours.
<n>88:43</n> Thou hast set up the right hand of them that oppress him: * thou hast made all his enemies to rejoice.
<n>88:44</n> Thou hast turned away the help of his sword; * and hast not assisted him in battle.
<n>88:45</n> Thou hast made his purification to cease: * and thou hast cast his throne down to the ground.
<n>88:46</n> Thou hast shortened the days of his time: * thou hast covered him with confusion.
<n>88:47</n> How long, O Lord, turnest thou away unto the end? * shall thy anger burn like fire?
<n>88:48</n> Remember what my substance is: * for hast thou made all the children of men in vain?
<n>88:49</n> Who is the man that shall live, and not see death: * that shall deliver his soul from the hand of hell?
<n>88:50</n> Lord, where are thy ancient mercies, * according to what thou didst swear to David in thy truth?
<n>88:51</n> Be mindful, O Lord, of the reproach of thy servants * which I have held in my bosom of many nations:
<n>88:52</n> Wherewith thy enemies have reproached, O Lord; * wherewith they have reproached the change of thy anointed.
<n>88:53</n> Blessed be the Lord for evermore. * So be it. So be it.
08.b730306a95:
<n>85:1</n> Inclína, Dómine, aurem tuam, et exáudi me: * quóniam inops, et pauper sum ego.
<n>85:2</n> Custódi ánimam meam, quóniam sanctus sum: * salvum fac servum tuum, Deus meus, sperántem in te.
<n>85:3</n> Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam ad te clamávi tota die: * lætífica ánimam servi tui, quóniam ad te, Dómine, ánimam meam levávi.
<n>85:5</n> Quóniam tu, Dómine, suávis, et mitis: * et multæ misericórdiæ ómnibus invocántibus te.
<n>85:6</n> Áuribus pércipe, Dómine, oratiónem meam: * et inténde voci deprecatiónis meæ.
<n>85:7</n> In die tribulatiónis meæ clamávi ad te: * quia exaudísti me.
<n>85:8</n> Non est símilis tui in diis, Dómine: * et non est secúndum ópera tua.
<n>85:9</n> Omnes gentes quascúmque fecísti, vénient, et adorábunt coram te, Dómine: * et glorificábunt nomen tuum.
<n>85:10</n> Quóniam magnus es tu, et fáciens mirabília: * tu es Deus solus.
<n>85:11</n> Deduc me, Dómine, in via tua, et ingrédiar in veritáte tua: * lætétur cor meum ut tímeat nomen tuum.
<n>85:12</n> Confitébor tibi, Dómine, Deus meus, in toto corde meo, * et glorificábo nomen tuum in ætérnum:
<n>85:13</n> Quia misericórdia tua magna est super me: * et eruísti ánimam meam ex inférno inferióri.
<n>85:14</n> Deus, iníqui insurrexérunt super me, et synagóga poténtium quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt te in conspéctu suo.
<n>85:15</n> Et tu, Dómine, Deus miserátor et miséricors, * pátiens, et multæ misericórdiæ, et verax,
<n>85:16</n> Réspice in me, et miserére mei, * da impérium tuum púero tuo: et salvum fac fílium ancíllæ tuæ.
<n>85:17</n> Fac mecum signum in bonum, ut vídeant qui odérunt me, et confundántur: * quóniam tu, Dómine, adjuvísti me, et consolátus es me.
08.160da512c7:
<n>85:1</n> Incline thy ear, O Lord, and hear me: * for I am needy and poor.
<n>85:2</n> Preserve my soul, for I am holy: * save thy servant, O my God, that trusteth in thee.
<n>85:3</n> Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I have cried to thee all the day. * Give joy to the soul of thy servant, for to thee, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul.
<n>85:5</n> For thou, O Lord, art sweet and mild: * and plenteous in mercy to all that call upon thee.
<n>85:6</n> Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer: * and attend to the voice of my petition.
<n>85:7</n> I have called upon thee in the day of my trouble: * because thou hast heard me.
<n>85:8</n> There is none among the gods like unto thee, O Lord: * and there is none according to thy works.
<n>85:9</n> All the nations thou hast made shall come and adore before thee, O Lord: * and they shall glorify thy name.
<n>85:10</n> For thou art great and dost wonderful things: * thou art God alone.
<n>85:11</n> Conduct me, O Lord, in thy way, and I will walk in thy truth: * let my heart rejoice that it may fear thy name.
<n>85:12</n> I will praise thee, O Lord my God, with my whole heart, * and I will glorify thy name for ever:
<n>85:13</n> For thy mercy is great towards me: * and thou hast delivered my soul out of the lower hell.
<n>85:14</n> O God, the wicked are risen up against me, and the assembly of the mighty have sought my soul: * and they have not set thee before their eyes.
<n>85:15</n> And thou, O Lord, art a God of compassion, and merciful, * patient, and of much mercy, and true.
<n>85:16</n> O look upon me, and have mercy on me: * give thy command to thy servant, and save the son of thy handmaid.
<n>85:17</n> Shew me a token for good: that they who hate me may see, and be confounded, * because thou, O Lord, hast helped me and hast comforted me.
08.cbb5142a90:
<n>87:2</n> Dómine, Deus salútis meæ: * in die clamávi, et nocte coram te.
<n>87:3</n> Intret in conspéctu tuo orátio mea: * inclína aurem tuam ad precem meam:
<n>87:4</n> Quia repléta est malis ánima mea: * et vita mea inférno appropinquávit.
<n>87:5</n> Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum: * factus sum sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
<n>87:6</n> Sicut vulneráti dormiéntes in sepúlcris, quorum non es memor ámplius: * et ipsi de manu tua repúlsi sunt.
<n>87:7</n> Posuérunt me in lacu inferióri: * in tenebrósis, et in umbra mortis.
<n>87:8</n> Super me confirmátus est furor tuus: * et omnes fluctus tuos induxísti super me.
<n>87:9</n> Longe fecísti notos meos a me: * posuérunt me abominatiónem sibi.
<n>87:9</n> Tráditus sum, et non egrediébar: * óculi mei languérunt præ inópia.
<n>87:10</n> Clamávi ad te, Dómine, tota die: * expándi ad te manus meas.
<n>87:11</n> Numquid mórtuis fácies mirabília: * aut médici suscitábunt, et confitebúntur tibi?
<n>87:12</n> Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro misericórdiam tuam, * et veritátem tuam in perditióne?
<n>87:13</n> Numquid cognoscéntur in ténebris mirabília tua, * et justítia tua in terra obliviónis?
<n>87:14</n> Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi: * et mane orátio mea prævéniet te.
<n>87:15</n> Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam: * avértis fáciem tuam a me?
<n>87:16</n> Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus a juventúte mea: * exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.
<n>87:17</n> In me transiérunt iræ tuæ: * et terróres tui conturbavérunt me.
<n>87:18</n> Circumdedérunt me sicut aqua tota die: * circumdedérunt me simul.
<n>87:19</n> Elongásti a me amícum et próximum: * et notos meos a miséria.
08.a05c5e676f:
<n>87:2</n> Lord, the God of my salvation: * I have cried in the day, and in the night before thee.
<n>87:3</n> Let my prayer come in before thee: * incline thy ear to my petition.
<n>87:4</n> For my soul is filled with evils: * and my life hath drawn nigh to hell.
<n>87:5</n> I am counted among them that go down to the pit: * I am become as a man without help, free among the dead.
<n>87:6</n> Like the slain sleeping in the sepulchres, whom thou rememberest no more: * and they are cast off from thy hand.
<n>87:7</n> They have laid me in the lower pit: * in the dark places, and in the shadow of death.
<n>87:8</n> Thy wrath is strong over me: * and all thy waves thou hast brought in upon me.
<n>87:9</n> Thou hast put away my acquaintance far from me: * they have set me an abomination to themselves.
<n>87:9</n> I was delivered up, and came not forth: * my eyes languished through poverty.
<n>87:10</n> All the day I cried to thee, O Lord: * I stretched out my hands to thee.
<n>87:11</n> Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? * or shall physicians raise to life, and give praise to thee?
<n>87:12</n> Shall any one in the sepulchre declare thy mercy: * and thy truth in destruction?
<n>87:13</n> Shall thy wonders be known in the dark; * and thy justice in the land of forgetfulness?
<n>87:14</n> But I, O Lord, have cried to thee: * and in the morning my prayer shall prevent thee.
<n>87:15</n> Lord, why castest thou off my prayer: * why turnest thou away thy face from me?
<n>87:16</n> I am poor, and in labours from my youth: * and being exalted have been humbled and troubled.
<n>87:17</n> Thy wrath hath come upon me: * and thy terrors have troubled me.
<n>87:18</n> They have come round about me like water all the day: * they have compassed me about together.
<n>87:19</n> Friend and neighbour thou hast put far from me: * and my acquaintance, because of misery.

<n>88:35</n> Neque profanábo testaméntum meum: * et quæ procédunt de lábiis meis, non fáciam írrita.
<n>88:36</n> Semel jurávi in sancto meo: Si David méntiar: * semen ejus in ætérnum manébit.
<n>88:37</n> Et thronus ejus sicut sol in conspéctu meo, * et sicut luna perfécta in ætérnum: et testis in cælo fidélis.

<n>88:31</n> And if his children forsake my law, * and walk not in my judgments:
<n>88:32</n> If they profane my justices: * and keep not my commandments:
<n>88:33</n> I will visit their iniquities with a rod: * and their sins with stripes.
<n>88:34</n> But my mercy I will not take away from him: * nor will I suffer my truth to fail.
<n>88:35</n> Neither will I profane my covenant: * and the words that proceed from my mouth I will not make void.
<n>88:36</n> Once have I sworn by my holiness: I will not lie unto David: * his seed shall endure for ever.
<n>88:37</n> And his throne as the sun before me: * and as the moon perfect for ever, and a faithful witness in heaven.
